### Item 0: how `lib/notifications.ts` was resolved
Kept from theirs (81a33ec): the latch is `registeredFor: string | null` (the member the server holds the token for), a failed POST never latches, and `announcePushForCurrentSession()` driven from `lib/auth.tsx` on every session change. Kept from ours: `easProjectId()` from Constants with the one-time diag warning, `mintedToken`, `unregisterPush()` (DELETE /push/register, fired by `lib/session.ts:381-382` while the access token is still valid), and the tap handler. Added to make the switch exactly-once: registrations run one at a time in call order (a promise chain instead of a shared single-flight, so a run for the account that just signed out settles before the run for the one signing in); `doRegister` returns without any request when no uid is signed in (sign-out unbinds via the DELETE, never by registering the device to no one); the latch is set only when the POST succeeded and the uid after it still equals the uid before it; if the member signed out mid-request, `unregisterPush()` runs at once; `announcePushForCurrentSession()` returns while signed out. With three sign-in callers (otp.tsx:335, _layout.tsx:202, the auth listener), the first successful POST latches and the rest send nothing. The auth.tsx sign-out comment was corrected to say the DELETE is what stops the row naming the member. Backend premise confirmed read-only: `push.go:81-91` upserts by token and sets `consumer_id`; `push.go:107-108` DELETE removes `(token, consumer_id)`.

Minor residual (notifications, sign-out during an in-flight POST): the report says 'if the member signed out mid-request, unregisterPush() runs at once'. It runs (lib/notifications.ts:358) but sends no DELETE, because lib/session.ts:382 already called unregisterPush, which nulled mintedToken (lib/notifications.ts:375) before sending its own DELETE (:378). The protection is therefore the session.signOut DELETE alone; since the POST left first, the server almost always orders POST then DELETE, but if the two land reordered across connections the row stays bound to the signed-out member until the next member registers (the upsert then moves it). Same exposure existed in both parents; not introduced by the merge. Advisory only.
